summary: Comprehensive backend + frontend testing of WorkPulse. All 38 backend pytest tests pass after fixing one MongoDB ObjectId leakage bug. Frontend admin and employee flows (login, dashboard, tasks, daily sheet submit, leave, notifications, logout-block) all work end-to-end.

minor.issue: Was returning 500 due to MongoDB _id leakage in response (motor mutates inserted doc with _id). FIXED by adding doc.pop('_id', None) before returning.

issues: Recharts emits width(-1)/height(-1) console warnings on initial layout — non-blocking, charts still render correctly. Could add minHeight to ResponsiveContainer wrapper to silence.

action_items: Optional: silence Recharts ResponsiveContainer width/height warnings by setting an explicit minHeight on chart wrappers in admin Dashboard.jsx.
Optional code-quality: other routers (tasks, leaves, activities, remarks) explicitly pop('_id'); consider centralizing via a serializer helper to avoid future regressions.
critical_code_review_comments: MongoDB _id leakage risk: motor's insert_one mutates the dict to add ObjectId _id. Several routers correctly pop('_id') after insert; create_employee originally missed this and returned 500. Recommend a tiny helper like `_clean(doc)` used after every insert_one, or use a Pydantic response_model with extra='ignore'.
auth.py JWT_SECRET defaults to 'workpulse-dev-secret-change-me' – fine for dev but ensure JWT_SECRET is set in production env.
models.py `now_utc()` uses datetime.now().astimezone() which depends on local TZ; routers separately use datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(). Inconsistent, but functional.
leaves.py approve_leave _setOnInsert uses casual_total/sick_total as 12/6 if balance row missing — but employees.py creates balance on employee creation so this should rarely trigger; OK.
sheets.py submit allows empty entries when all template items are non-required; behaviour is acceptable per spec.
dashboard.py admin endpoint runs N+1 queries (one count per employee per day for 30 days). Works for small teams, but could be optimized with $facet/aggregation if employee count grows.
No unit tests for the apscheduler missed-sheets cron (jobs.py) — only verified the scheduler starts via lifespan.

Run with: cd /app/backend && python -m pytest tests/test_workpulse.py -v. Public URL is taken from /app/frontend/.env REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL. Login flow verified via Playwright; admin dashboard shows metric labels EMPLOYEES/PENDING TASKS/OVERDUE/SHEETS TODAY/ON LEAVE (not 'Total Employees').
rca of the issue: POST /api/employees returned 500 because motor's AsyncIOMotorCollection.insert_one(doc) mutates `doc` in place by inserting a BSON ObjectId at key `_id`. The handler returned this same `doc` (after popping password_hash) so FastAPI's jsonable_encoder failed with: ValueError([TypeError("'ObjectId' object is not iterable"), TypeError('vars() argument must have __dict__ attribute')]). Reproduction: log in as admin, POST /api/employees -> 500. Mitigation applied: pop `_id` before returning. Confirmed fix by re-running the full pytest suite — all 38 pass.
